blocks.label: The short of it

blocks.html:
The recommendation

Three things, in the order we'd do them. Nothing here is a rebuild from scratch: your flows work, they just stop early and one of them is pointed at the wrong list.

  1. Double the campaigns, 4 a month to 8. $300 each, so $1,200 a month more. Your own weeks say it's worth $97,679 to $195,358 a year.
  2. Add 8 emails to the automations you already have, and fix the welcome trigger. A one-off $2,400. Worth about $98,803 a year, then it runs for nothing.
  3. Rebuild the sign-up form, then keep testing it. $500 a month. At 0.49% it is the cheapest number in the account to move, and moving it to 1.0% is worth $21,558 a year.

1. Your campaigns are under-sent

Over 52 weeks, May ’25 to Oct ’26, you sent one campaign in 40 ordinary weeks and two in 5. The one-send weeks earned $6,494. The two-send weeks earned $10,564. The second send earns a bit less on its own ($5,282 against $6,494), so there is some overlap, but it adds 81% of a campaign rather than splitting one in half.

blocks.note: The rate per send actually falls, 0.29% to 0.22%, because you are reaching the same people more efficiently. The count still goes up, and across 48 extra campaigns that is roughly 1,300 more unsubscribes a year. Worth naming before you decide, not after. Black Friday week Nov ’25 is the same at full stretch: 5 campaigns, $35,727, 127 unsubscribes against a normal week's 38, and still the lowest rate on the board at 0.19%.

blocks.html:
2. Your flows work. They are just short

Four flows, all of them earning. Here's what each one makes every time it sends an email, what sets it off, and where it stops.

The welcome is pointed at one of your two sign-up lists. It fires on Master List, which took 472 people this year. 992 more joined Newsletter and got nothing. Pointing it at both is worth $35,941 a year before a single new email is written.

The one called Onboarding is really your post-purchase series. It fires on an order, sends 5 emails, and stops on day 16. But 6,856 people bought last year and placed 7,408 orders, so only 552 came back. On a $737 order, the second and third purchase happen long after day 16, and nothing of yours is there.

Which eight, and why those eight

We run 18 Klaviyo accounts. Before writing a line of this we ranked 277 of their automations by what one email in each is actually worth. Subscription billing reminders are left out: they earn more than anything else per send and prove nothing about marketing. Each bar below is the middle account, not the best one, and everything is shown against a post-purchase email, which is the kind we were going to put three of yours into.

Abandonment wins, and it is not close. An abandoned-checkout email is worth 8 times a post-purchase one. Your own account says the same thing even louder: $29 an email against $5. So the three we were going to put after day 16 go to the cart instead.

What we are not doing yet. Back-in-stock is the best email in our book, and your store has never recorded a single back-in-stock sign-up, so there is nothing to trigger on. The post-purchase gap after day 16 is real and we still want it. Both are the next conversation, not this one.

blocks.note: Plus the welcome trigger fix, which costs nothing to write.

3. The sign-up form is the cheapest number to move

Everything above works on the people you already have. This is the only line that adds more of them.

blocks.note: We'd rebuild it once and then keep testing it, month after month: offer, timing, wording, mobile against desktop. Getting to 1.0% is about 1,476 extra subscribers a year, worth $21,558 at half what a subscriber earns you today. It's also the only part of this that gets better the longer it runs.

What doing nothing costs, and what doing half of it costs

blocks.note: Campaigns earn money from the list you have. They don't build it, and at 8 a month they spend it faster: add the 1,300 extra unsubscribes from part one and the net loss is nearer 1,759 a year.
blocks.label: Your email list, last 12 months

blocks.html: That is why the three parts belong together. The campaigns earn more from the list, the flows earn more from each person on it, and the sign-up form is the only thing that refills it. Take the first on its own and you are spending an asset faster without topping it up. You are also at 27,382 of your 28,000 Klaviyo profiles, so the people you keep need to be worth more, not just more numerous.

What it asks of your team

  • Nothing for the flows. We write them, you approve them once, they run by themselves from then on.
  • No new approvals process for the campaigns. Same monthly batch, twice the emails in it.
  • Nothing for the testing. It happens on your site, we report what won, you never have to look at it unless you want to.
  • No commitment to fill the calendar. 8 is a ceiling we're allowed to use, not a quota. If revenue per campaign or unsubscribes move the wrong way we drop back, and you've learned where your ceiling is.

Campaigns. 52 weeks of your own sends, May ’25 to Oct ’26, grouped by how many went out that week. 7 offer weeks and 3 peak weeks are excluded, so it is ordinary week against ordinary week and a sale can't inflate the step. A cadence is only quoted where you ran it at least three times.

The unsubscribe count. Your two-send weeks also went to a slightly wider audience per send (15,573 against 13,884), so part of the extra 28 is reach rather than frequency. We have left it all in the frequency column, which makes 1,300 a year the pessimistic reading.

The added emails. Each one is priced at a quarter of what the flow it joins already earns per email: half because last-click attribution is generous, half again because the sixth email in a series never performs like the first. Pointing the welcome at both lists is priced at half rather than a quarter, because those emails are already written and already performing; they are simply not being sent to everyone. Every volume is discounted 25% for people who buy, leave or drop out of a series part way.

The form. Views and submissions are Klaviyo form events for the 12 months to 31 Oct 2026. A subscriber is valued at the $29 a year your email programme earns per active profile, then halved. Order, customer and list figures are Klaviyo events over the same window, read from your account when this page was built.

Revenue is Klaviyo's attribution on last click, the generous reading rather than the strict one. That is why everything here is quoted at half or less, and the case still stands there. A holdout test gives you the strict number and we will run one if you want it.

reports.summary: Send more, finish the automations you already have, and fix a sign-up form converting at 0.49%. $22,800 in year one against $218,040, every figure taken at half of what your account already earns or less.
